title: Shams and the Unlit Lantern
logline: Shams tries to give light to Salma and learns you can only share a flame you carry.
story: Salma, who was one with deep rhythm, lived in fear of the dark, and Shams, who carried the sun's radiance, arrived with a grand offer of light. But Shams's own lantern was cold, kept only for show. However many times Shams pressed the dead lamp into Salma's hands, no warmth would pass. Only when Shams stopped to kindle a true flame within did the smallest glow leap, at last, from one wick to the other. Shams learned that light is never given from an empty hand.
moral: You cannot give a light you have not first kindled within yourself.
